1.note: These two clauses mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [Bel and Nebo both bow low]
The words **Bel** and **Nebo** are the names of Babylonian gods.

The implication is that the images of these gods are being loaded onto the pack animals to be carried away into captivity. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [their images are loaded onto animals and beasts]
The pronoun **your** refers to the people of Babylon, whose idols these are. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Babylon’s carried things are loaded]

The expression **loaded** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [they have loaded your carried things]

Isaiah is using the adjective **weary** as a noun to mean a certain kind of animal. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [to those who are weary]

2.note: The terms **stooped** and **bowed down** mean similar things. Isaiah is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [They completely bowed down together]
The pronoun **They** refers to the idols of Bel and Nebo. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [The idols of Bel and Nebo stooped]

The implication is that these gods could not even save their own images, which are the burden being carried away. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [they were not able to rescue even their own images]

Isaiah is speaking as if these idols each had a **soul**, and he is using that part of them to mean all of them. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and they have gone]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **captivity**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [away as captives]

3.note: Here, **house of Jacob** represents “the people who are descended from Jacob.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the people descended from Jacob]

Here, **the house of Israel** represents “the people who are descended from Israel.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the people of Israel]

The terms **house of Jacob** and **house of Israel** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [those remaining of the descendants of Jacob, who is Israel]

The terms **the ones loaded from the belly** and **the ones carried from the womb** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [you who I have carried since your birth]

4.note: Yahweh is stating the pronoun **I** separately, even though the verb translated as **I will bear** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize his commitment to uphold Israel. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [I myself will bear you]

If the connection between this statement and the previous one is not clear, you may want to use a different connecting word to show how this statement relates to what comes before it. Alternate translation: [And because I, Yahweh, made you, I myself will bear you]

For poetic purposes, Isaiah is using two different words that have basically the same meaning. The ULT translates the one here as **carry** and the one in verses 1 and 3 as “carried” because English does not have two different words that it can use in this context. But if your language does, it would be appropriate to use them here.

5.note: Yahweh is using the question form to assert that there is no one who can be compared to him. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [There is no one to whom you can liken me, that you should equate me, and no one to whom you can compare me, that we should resemble.]

6.note: By **The ones dumping gold**, Isaiah means that people who want an idol pour out gold freely and lavishly to pay for their idol to be made. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [To obtain an idol to worship, the people lavishly pouring out gold]
The phrase **The ones** refers to people in general who make idols to worship. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [The people dumping gold]

The implication is that the object they make is merely a manufactured image, even though they call it a god and worship it. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and they make it into an idol that they call a god]

The pronoun **it** refers to the **gold** and **silver** that they provided to the metalworker. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and the metalworker makes the metals]

7.note: The pronoun **They** refers to the people who make and worship the idol. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [The people who make the idol lift it]

Isaiah is speaking of the idol as if it were a living thing that could **stand** and **depart**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and it remains there; it does not move from its place]

If the connection between this statement and the previous one is not clear, you may want to use a different connecting word to show how this statement relates to what comes before it. Alternate translation: [And one cries out to it]

Isaiah uses the word **but** here to indicate a contrast between all that people do to set up and call upon the idol and the idol’s complete inability to answer or save them. In your translation, indicate this contrast in a way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [yet it does not answer]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **trouble**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [from the difficult situation he is in]

8.note: Yahweh is using the phrase **return {it}, rebelling ones, to the heart** as a common expression of the culture to mean “think carefully about this.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [think carefully about this, you rebels]

The pronoun **it** refers to what Yahweh is telling the people to remember, namely that he alone is God. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [return the truth that I alone am God]

9.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **eternity**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [from before time began]

9.q: כִּ֣י אָנֹכִ֥י אֵל֙ וְ⁠אֵ֣ין ע֔וֹד אֱלֹהִ֖ים וְ⁠אֶ֥פֶס כָּמֽוֹ⁠נִי
9.note: These two clauses mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could connect the phrases with a word other than **and** in order to show that the second phrase is repeating the first one, not saying something additional. Alternate translation: [for I am God and there is no other; indeed, none is like me]

In the phrase **God, and none is like me**, God is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [I am God, and none is like me]

10.note: Yahweh is referring to all of history by naming its two major components, **the end** and **the beginning**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [declaring what will happen from beginning to end]

The expression **have not been done** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [what has not yet happened]

Yahweh is speaking of his **counsel** as if it were a living thing that could **stand**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [My counsel will be established]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **counsel**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [What I have decided]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **desire**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [what I want]

11.note: Yahweh is using **the rising {of the sun}** as a common expression of the culture to mean “the east.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [from the eastern direction]

Yahweh is speaking of the conqueror he will summon as if he were **a bird of prey**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [one who will quickly defeat his enemies]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **land** that is characterized by being far away. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [from a faraway land]

The implication is that this is the man whom Yahweh has chosen to carry out his plan. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the man whom I have chosen to carry out my plan]
See how you translated the similar expression in 46:10.

If the connection between this statement and the previous one is not clear, you may want to use a different connecting word to show how this statement relates to what comes before it. Alternate translation: [Surely, I have spoken]

Yahweh is repeating the word **Indeed** in order to strongly intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [Surely, I have spoken; certainly, I will make it come about. I have formed it; You can be sure that I will do it]

12.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 46:3.

Yahweh is using the adjective phrase **strong of heart** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [you who are strong of heart] or [you stubborn-hearted people]

Yahweh is using **far from righteousness** as a common expression of the culture to mean “refusing to do what is right.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [those who refuse to do what is right]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **righteousness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [far from right behavior]

13.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **righteousness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [my righteous acts]

Yahweh is speaking of his righteousness as if it were an object that could be **far** away in distance. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [it will come soon]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **salvation**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and my rescuing you]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **salvation**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [And I will give rescue]

Here, **Zion** represents “the people who live in Zion.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [among the people of Zion]

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [I will give my splendor to Israel]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **splendor**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [my glorious presence]
Here, **Israel** represents “the people of Israel.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [to the people of Israel]
